page.title: Manage your website with AI
page.description: Tess has a built-in MCP server: let Claude, Cursor or any MCP client create, edit and publish your content in plain language, safely.

sections.title: Your website, managed by talking to your AI.
sections.subtitle: Tess speaks the **Model Context Protocol**, the open standard AI assistants use to work with tools. Connect Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Pi or any MCP client in two minutes, then ask in plain language: *“draft a post about our new release”*, *“fix the typos on the pricing page”*, *“which products have no image?”*. No plugin to install, no code to write.
sections.code:
You: Find every published post without a meta
     description and write one for each, as drafts.

AI:  Found 12 posts. I've drafted a description
     for each one and submitted them for review.

You: Add a "Summer sale" banner to the home page
     for next week, and show me the draft.

sections.title: What you can ask
sections.body:
Your assistant reads your content models first, so it knows your fields, relations and components without any setup. Then it works like an editor who never gets tired:

- **Write:** *“Draft three blog posts from these release notes, with a summary and tags.”*
- **Edit at scale:** *“Every product description over 300 words: shorten it and keep the tone.”*
- **Check:** *“Which published pages have no meta description or no cover image?”*
- **Model:** *“Add an FAQ content type with a question, an answer and a category.”* (with an Admin token)
- **Publish:** *“Publish the drafts I approved this morning.”*
- **Answer questions:** *“How many articles did we publish per month this year?”*

It works with every content model you create, the moment you create it: the MCP server exposes your whole GraphQL API through two generic tools, `get_schema` and `graphql_query`.

sections.title: Set up in two minutes
sections.body:
1. **Turn it on** in your server settings: `TESS_MCP=true`.
2. **Create an API token** for your assistant in the admin (**API tokens**), with the role it needs: Contributor to write drafts, Member to read only.
3. **Add Tess to your AI client**: the URL of your server, and the token in an `Authorization: Bearer` header, as shown here. Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex and Pi each take it in one line of their configuration.

That's it: your assistant now sees your content, with exactly the rights of its token. For clients that only run local programs, like Claude Desktop, the `tess mcp` command does the same through a small local proxy.

[Read the MCP guide →](/docs/developers/mcp)

sections.title: AI that works for you, not around you
sections.body:
Giving an AI access to your website should not mean giving up control. With Tess it doesn't:

- **The same rules as everyone.** The assistant uses an API token, and Tess applies that token's role and scope to every call. A Member token reads; a Contributor token writes drafts, only on the content types you allow.
- **Humans keep the last word.** With review workflows, the AI's changes are drafts submitted for review: your team approves them before anything goes live.
- **Everything is traced.** Each change records who made it, so you always know what the assistant did, and can revoke its token in one click.
- **Your data stays yours.** Tess runs on your servers and talks only to the AI client you connect, with only the content its token can reach.

items.question: Which AI tools work with Tess?
items.answer: Any client that supports the Model Context Protocol: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, OpenCode, Codex, Pi, Cursor and more. Clients that support remote servers connect to `https://your-server/mcp` directly, with your API token in an `Authorization: Bearer` header; others, like Claude Desktop, run the local `tess mcp` proxy. The [MCP guide](/docs/developers/mcp) has the configuration of each one.

items.question: How does my AI assistant sign in to Tess?
items.answer: With an API token you create in the admin. The client sends it in the `Authorization: Bearer` header of every request, so Tess knows which token, and which role, is calling. Keep it in an environment variable rather than in a config file, and revoke it in one click if needed. Without a token, an assistant can only read published content.

items.question: Is the MCP server part of the Community edition?
items.answer: Yes. It's built into Tess, in every edition: no add-on, no extra service. It's off until you set `TESS_MCP=true`.

items.question: Can the AI delete or break my content?
items.answer: Only if you give it a token that allows it. Use a Contributor token scoped to a few content types, and enable review workflows: the AI then writes drafts that your team reviews and publishes.

items.question: Does it work with my own content models?
items.answer: Yes, with all of them, as soon as you create them. The assistant reads your schema first, so there is nothing to configure per model.

sections.title: Let your AI run the busywork

features.title: Run it with AI
features.summary: A built-in MCP server lets Claude, Cursor and any MCP client read your models and create, edit and publish content in plain language, with the same permissions as the API.

features.title: Models at runtime
features.summary: Create content types in the admin or through the API, in production. The GraphQL schema is regenerated on the fly: no rebuild, no redeploy.

features.title: GraphQL-first
features.summary: Typed queries, filters, sorting, pagination, relations and mutations generated for every model, with a GraphiQL IDE built in.

features.title: Your database
features.summary: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, DynamoDB or embedded RocksDB. Every backend passes the same conformance suite.

features.title: Review workflows
features.summary: Draft and publish for every entry, plus an optional submit → approve workflow per content type, in every edition.

features.title: Roles and scoped tokens
features.summary: Owner, Admin, Contributor, Reviewer and Member roles, limited to some content types if needed, and scoped API tokens for machines.

features.title: Sandboxed plugins
features.summary: WebAssembly plugins installed by admins at runtime, written in Rust, Go, JavaScript and more, with timeouts and memory limits.

features.title: Serverless or container
features.summary: One binary runs as an HTTP server (Docker, VM, Kubernetes) or as an AWS Lambda function.

features.title: Media library
features.summary: Uploads to S3-compatible stores (Garage, MinIO, AWS S3, Cloudflare R2) or the local filesystem, with direct presigned uploads.

features.title: Full-text search
features.summary: Typesense indexing kept in sync with your content, behind a pluggable search engine interface.

features.title: Private by design
features.summary: Opaque, expiring, encrypted ids in the API: database ids never leave the server.

features.title: Portable models
features.summary: tess-transfer exports content models and users to YAML or JSON, to version them or copy them between instances.

competitors.name: Strapi
competitors.summary: The most popular open-source headless CMS, built on Node.js, with a REST API and a GraphQL plugin.

competitors.name: Hygraph
competitors.summary: A hosted, GraphQL-native CMS (formerly GraphCMS), known for content federation across remote APIs.

competitors.name: WordPress
competitors.summary: The world's most used CMS, a PHP application with themes, plugins and a REST API, often used headless through WPGraphQL.

competitors.name: Contentful
competitors.summary: An enterprise headless CMS delivered as SaaS, with REST and GraphQL delivery APIs and a large app ecosystem.

competitors.name: Directus
competitors.summary: A Node.js platform that turns an existing SQL database into REST and GraphQL APIs with an admin app.

competitors.name: Payload
competitors.summary: An open-source TypeScript CMS configured in code, which installs inside a Next.js application.

competitors.name: Sanity
competitors.kind: Hosted content platform with an open-source studio
competitors.summary: A hosted Content Lake with a customizable, open-source React editing studio and its own query language, GROQ.
